finding: The historical Free-Swarm legacy source_event_id preimage binds the concrete source_path. A cumulative line checkpoint removes resume-dependent line-number drift but cannot make that event identity stable across relocation of the same artifact tree to a different absolute artifact root.
counterhypothesis: Artifact-root-relative logical paths remove absolute-root relocation drift but do not establish fully path-independent occurrence identity when the same worker row is re-homed under a different logical run directory. A stronger future successor may require an immutable producer run identity if such identity is present or historically recoverable.
decision: Add a successor causal_event_id under CLAY_FREE_SWARM_CAUSAL_EVENT_IDENTITY/v2 while preserving legacy source_event_id as compatibility/admission identity. Do not silently reinterpret existing hashes, rows, chunks, candidate provenance, or receipts.

deterministic_local_source_test.command_class: python unittest on pre-commit content-equivalent helper/test files

acceptance_discriminators: same artifact tree relocated under a different absolute artifact root yields the same v2 causal_event_id
one-shot and resumed scans yield identical absolute-line plus v2 causal identity
legacy admission identity may differ while relocated v2 causal identity remains equal
different logical run paths remain distinct
replay of one v2 causal event adds zero source-support weight after first admission
mixed legacy/v2 migration fails closed for v2-derived support credit
second saturation pass creates zero new causal IDs, support, packets, and accepted dataset tokens

external_donor_check.principle: event identity is producer/source scoped and replayed duplicates may retain the same id; transport destination is not event identity
external_donor_check.use: design corroboration only; not canonical Clay authority
